name: MIT Battlecode 2027
applications_open: Register ~early Jan 2027; season runs all January, ends ~Jan 31
notes: MIT's real-time strategy AI competition: you write an autonomous player that commands a robot army, then compete in scrimmages and bracketed tournaments over January. Over $20,000 in total prize money. Open beyond MIT - 'Anyone can write a bot, create a team, and participate in scrimmage matches/rankings.' Prize-tournament gates from the Full Eligibility Rules (battlecode.org/about.html): Sprint Tournaments - 'All teams are eligible.' US Qualifier - 'Teams must consist entirely of US college students studying full-time, or in a transition phase.' Final Tournament - 'Teams must have qualified via the US or International Qualifier.' MIT Newbie Tournament is MIT-only and High School Tournament is high-school-only, so neither applies. Unlike MIT Pokerbots, no MIT-affiliated teammate or MIT certificate is needed for the track you would enter. As of Sep 2026 the site still reads 'Battlecode 2026 ended on January 31st, 2026!' - no 2027 registration date posted yet, though the page already references Battlecode 2027 sponsorships. No team size limit, age limit, or citizenship rule beyond 'US college student' was stated on the pages read. Source: battlecode.org home page and about.html.

IMPORTANT, the obvious URL is the wrong one: www.morganstanley.com/careers/career-opportunities-search sits behind an Akamai WAF that resets the connection for paths.USER_AGENT and returns HTTP 200 with 134KB to a spoofed Chrome string - same machine, same IP, so the block is User-Agent based and it is the Citadel case, reachable only by misrepresenting the client. Do not re-point a source at it. Morgan Stanley's OTHER board, morganstanley.eightfold.ai, is reachable honestly via /api/pcsx/search but is deliberately NOT watched: it carries 1,327 corporate roles, caps page size at 10 (about 133 requests a day), and a query for 'Sophomore' or 'Freshman' returns zero - the campus programmes are not on it. Probed 2026-09-18: 9,660 chars of visible text, ratio 0.063, allowed by robots.txt (crawl-delay 10; the named-bot block covers ClaudeBot/GPTBot, not this tracker's own UA), no redirect.
